{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement (Kubient / The Associated Press)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel 
**Re:** Playbook review of Master Services Agreement, dated 5 February (Exhibit 10.14) — we represent the Customer (AP) 
**Status:** 18 rules assessed — 8 compliant, 7 deviations, 3 missing

---

## Executive summary

On balance this is a favourable paper for us, and several of the terms we most often have to fight for are simply absent: there is no exclusivity, no non-compete, no minimum commitment, no MFN, no non-solicit, no liquidated damages or exit fee, and no Vendor audit right running against us. Section 1 affirmatively preserves our freedom to offer Inventory through other agents or directly to third parties, and the Vendor indemnity in Section 10(a) is broad and — because Section 7(a) carves indemnification out of the damages waiver — uncapped in our favour.

Our priority issue is the mirror image of that last point. Section 7 is the only liability provision in the Agreement and contains **no aggregate cap of any kind**, so our own direct exposure is unlimited. We are asking for a mutual 12-month fees cap with the usual carve-outs, on a "paid or payable under this Agreement" basis because Section 5 operates as a revenue share and a Customer-paid-fees measure would be illusory.

Three structural gaps also need closing. There is **no IP or data-ownership article**: we receive no licence to deliverables and there is no limit on Kubient's use of our Content, Requests or visitor data. There is **no transition assistance or data-return obligation** — Section 4(c) revokes our access and stops the Services with no exit runway. And the licence in Section 2 is non-transferable and personal to AP alone, so it neither reaches our affiliates nor survives an M&A event. Separately, the dispute mechanics are internally inconsistent: Section 14(a) fixes Delaware law with exclusive New York court venue, while Section 8 mandates AAA arbitration.

Remaining items are shorter-form: Kubient can terminate for convenience mid-term, the first renewal cannot be avoided, the assignment carve-out is mutual (letting Kubient move the contract to any affiliate or successor, including a competitor), there is no software conformance warranty or warranty remedy, and there is no insurance covenant.

---

## Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | Preamble | Exceeds fallback: broad Vendor defend/indemnify duty (§10(a)) read with §9(b) warranties; standard §11 procedure; no super-cap and no IP carve-outs. Affiliates not named as indemnitees and our §10(b) indemnity is wider than preferred — noted only. |
| 2 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | Preamble | §7 has a mutual consequential-damages waiver but no aggregate cap; our direct liability is unlimited. Proposal: mutual 12-month fees cap with indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct outside it. |
| 3 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment / change of control | **Deviation** | Preamble | Para (h) carve-out is mutual, so Kubient may assign to any affiliate or successor — including an AP competitor — without consent. Proposal: Customer-only carve-out, competitor bar, and confirmation of no Kubient termination right on our change of control. |
| 4 | High | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Missing** | Preamble | No IP/data article. Our platform licence is revocable and we hold no licence to deliverables; no limit on Kubient's use of our data. Proposal at fallback: Kubient keeps tools/platform; we get a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free deliverables licence with modification and sublicensing rights; Kubient's data licence limited to providing the Services. |
| 5 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | Preamble | §2 grant runs to AP alone and is expressly non-transferable/non-assignable, with §6(a) barring third-party access; the licence would be stranded on an M&A event. Proposal: extend to affiliates on written notice and make transferable to an M&A successor. |
| 6 | High | EXCLUSIVITY | Compliant | Preamble | §1 expressly disclaims exclusivity; Kubient's licence to us is non-exclusive. §5 contracting role is scoped to Platform delivery and subject to our §1 freedom. |
| 7 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties on Customer | Compliant | Preamble | No LDs, penalties, minimum-fee-on-termination or exit fee payable by us; §4(a) exit requires notice only. |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE | Compliant | Preamble | No non-compete, field-of-use or territory covenant on us; only ordinary licence-use limits in §6(a). |
| 9 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Deviation** | Preamble | §14(a) pairs Delaware law with exclusive New York venue, and §8 mandates AAA arbitration, displacing that venue. Proposal: New York law, exclusive New York County courts, delete the arbitration sentence (jury waiver and one-year limitation retained). |
| 10 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal / non-renewal window | **Deviation** | Preamble | §4(a) auto-renews for successive 1-year terms; the for-any-reason exit is available only after the Initial Term on 90 days' notice, so the first renewal cannot be avoided and the window exceeds 60 days. Proposal: Customer non-renewal right on 60 days' notice. *(Finding verification: repaired.)* |
| 11 | Medium | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Deviation** | Preamble | Our 90-day exit is within the fallback band, but Kubient may also terminate for any reason mid-term. Proposal: Kubient's for-any-reason termination effective only at the end of the then-current Term. |
| 12 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance / data return | **Missing** | Preamble | §4(c) only ceases Services, revokes the licence and returns Confidential Information; no transition assistance and no data export. Proposal at fallback: 90 days' transition assistance and data export within 30 days. |
| 13 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | Preamble | §9(b) ongoing Service warranties run for the Term and are preserved by the §13 disclaimer, but there is no conformance-to-documentation warranty and no warranty remedy anywhere. Proposal: 90-day software conformance warranty plus repair/replace/refund. |
| 14 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | Preamble | No Vendor audit, inspection or records right against us; the §1 access obligation is service-delivery cooperation only. Better than preferred; adding machinery would create a right that does not exist. |
| 15 | Medium | MFN | Compliant | Preamble | No MFN, "no less favorable", best-terms or right-to-match obligation on us. |
| 16 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume limits | Compliant | Preamble | §5 is a pure revenue share on amounts actually generated; §4(a) captures only fees actually generated during the notice period; §13 confirms no guaranteed revenue level. |
| 17 | Medium | NOSOLICIT | Compliant | Preamble | No non-solicit, no-hire or non-poach covenant binds us, and none survives termination. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | Preamble | No insurance covenant anywhere, despite Kubient's §9(b)(iii) undertaking on collection, management and storage of visitor data. Proposal: E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M as a new general provision. |

---

## Walk-away items

None of the findings was classified as walk-away, and no term in the Agreement is disqualifying on its face.

We would, however, treat the following as must-fix before signature, in this order:

1. **Liability cap (LOL-CAP, critical).** Unlimited direct exposure with no cap of any kind is not a position we can accept; a mutual 12-month fees cap is the minimum.
2. **IP and data ownership (IP, high, missing).** We need a deliverables licence and a use limitation on our Content, Requests and visitor data.
3. **Transition assistance and data return (TRANSITION, medium, missing).** Today termination cuts our access with no exit runway and no right to get our data back.

---

## Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the seven deviations and three gaps above, with each edit carrying a `[Playbook]` comment stating the position and, where relevant, the fallback we are accepting.
2. **Confirm the commercial premise for the cap wording** — we drafted "fees paid or payable under this Agreement" rather than "by Customer" because §5 is a revenue share; deal team to confirm that reflects the intended money flow.
3. **Resolve the §8 / §14(a) conflict as a drafting point first.** The arbitration and exclusive-venue clauses contradict each other, which gives us a clean, non-adversarial route to the New York law/New York County package.
4. **Do not reopen the favourable terms.** We will not trade away the uncapped Vendor indemnity, the absence of exclusivity, minimum commitments, MFN, non-solicit or Vendor audit rights, and we will not concede the mutuality of the assignment carve-out by surrendering our own.
5. **Flag for the file:** if Kubient later proposes audit or non-solicit language, we hold prepared fallback parameters (annual audit, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, no system access; mutual 12-month non-solicit limited to services personnel with advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs)."}
